Description: These are the most basic SQL queries that retrieve data from a single table without any complex conditions or joins.
These queries include simple filtering criteria like WHERE clauses with one or two conditions.
Example: SELECT * FROM my_table WHERE column1 = 'value' AND column2 > 10;

Description: These queries involve grouping and aggregating data using functions such as COUNT, SUM, AVG, MIN, and MAX.
Example: SELECT column1, COUNT(*) FROM my_table GROUP BY column1;

Description: These queries involve nesting one query inside another. Subqueries can be used in many ways, such as filtering, joining, or performing calculations on the results of the inner query.
Example: SELECT * FROM my_table WHERE column1 IN (SELECT column1 FROM another_table WHERE column2 = 'value');

Description: These queries involve joining multiple tables together and may include multiple levels of subqueries and complex conditions. These queries require a deeper understanding of SQL syntax and data modeling
Example: SELECT t1.*, t2.* FROM table1 t1 JOIN table2 t2 ON t1.id = t2.table1_id WHERE t1.column1 = 'value' AND t2.column2 > 10 GROUP BY t1.column1, t2.column2 HAVING COUNT(*) > 1 ORDER BY t1.column1 ASC, t2.column2 DESC;
